name: TerminalPairing
documentation: A TerminalPairing is a standard reference setup of exactly two terminals and a defined length of a core contacted to both terminals. The TerminalPairing defines physical properties that apply to this combination (e.g. contactResistance) . Other values might be independent from a specific conductor (e.g. matingForce ). Therefore, the referencedCoreSpecification is optional.

attributes.name: contactResistance
attributes.doc: Specifies the resistance of the terminal pairing.

attributes.name: matingForce
attributes.doc: Specifies the joining force of the two terminals.

attributes.name: unmatingForce
attributes.doc: Specifies the force required to unmate the two terminals.

attributes.name: matingCycles
attributes.doc: The maximum number of mating cycles, this terminal combination is certified for.

name: TerminalPairingSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of TerminalPairings.

name: CavityMounting
documentation: A CavityMounting defines the cavities (CavityReference) where the contacted elements (Terminal) will be mounted.

name: CavityMountingDetail
documentation: With a CavityMountingDetail it is possible to describe a detailed cavity mounting. This is needed if the information which terminal reception is mounted into which cavity is important. There are cases where this information can be relevant (e.g. bridge contacts with an asymmetric wire mounting).

name: ContactPoint
documentation: A contact point defines the relationship between Terminals, Seals, Plugs, Cavities and Wires. It specifies a single contacting variant. This means that the contacting is manufactured, as specified by the Contact Point. Either all participants (Cavities, Terminals, Seals, Wires) set into a relationship by the ContactPoint exist in a specific harness or none. There is no requirement, to filter the participants of a contacting situation with information derived from VariantConfigurations or assembl

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the ContactPoint. The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the ContactingSpecification.

name: ContactingSpecification
documentation: Specification for the description of the contacting. A contacting defines the relationships between Terminals, Seals, Plugs, Cavities and Wires.

name: WireMounting
documentation: A WireMounting defines the mounting of a wire end to terminal. If the contacting is required to be waterproof a cavity seal can be mounted additionally.

name: WireMountingDetail
documentation: With a WireMountingDetail it is possible to describe a detailed wire mounting. This is needed if the information which wire end is mounted onto which wire reception is important (e.g. coax contacts).

attributes.name: coreCrimpSize
attributes.doc: Defines the required core crimp size (width & height) of this specific wire mounting situation.

attributes.name: insulationCrimpSize
attributes.doc: Defines the required insulation crimp size (width & height) of this specific wire mounting situation.

attributes.name: wireTipProtrusion
attributes.doc: Defines the valid length range in which the protrusion of the conductor from the conductor crimp must be located.

attributes.name: wireReceptionType
attributes.doc: Defines the joining method to be applied for this WireMountingDetail. This is particularly relevant for wire receptions that support multiple joining methods (see WireReceptionSpecification.WireRecept

attributes.name: absoluteSealPosition
attributes.doc: The absoluteSealPosition defines the distance between the conductor tip and edge of the CavitySeal facing the conductor tip.

attributes.name: pullOffForce
attributes.doc: The minimum force, of this specific wire mounting situation, that the completed crimp should withstand when the wire is being pulled off the terminal. Above that force, the crimp can be expected to be

attributes.name: corePullOffForce
attributes.doc: The minimum force, of this specific wire mounting situation, that the completed crimp should withstand when the wire is being pulled off the terminal. Above that force, the crimp can be expected to be

attributes.name: insulationPullOffForce
attributes.doc: The minimum force, of this specific wire mounting situation, that the completed crimp should withstand when the wire is being pulled off the terminal. Above that force, the crimp can be expected to be

name: AliasIdentification
documentation: Class for the definition of alias identifications. Alias identifications are additional identifications for VEC-elements, which are valid in a certain scope (e.g. PPS-ID's).

attributes.name: identificationValue
attributes.doc: Specifies the identification value.

attributes.name: type
attributes.doc: Defines the type (or the role) of the AliasIdentification. Defined literals are contained in an OpenEnumeration.

attributes.name: scope
attributes.doc: The scope in which the AliasIdentification is valid / or the issuer of the alias id. This could be for example a certain process, a company or an IT-System.

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: On optional human readable description of the AliasIdentification.

name: ConfigurableElement
documentation: Abstract base class for all elements which can be configured with a VariantConfiguration.

name: DocumentVersion
documentation: A DocumentVersion is a unique identifier for a piece of information in a company context. The DocumentVersion is one of the three anchors for PDM information in the VEC. All technical information about a PartVersion is contained in one or more documents. The documents are containing the actual content of the VEC since all Specifications are an element of a document.

attributes.name: documentNumber
attributes.doc: The documentNumber is the major identifier of a DocumentVersion. The format is user defined and respectively company specific.

attributes.name: documentType
attributes.doc: The type of the document, which is defined in an OpenEnumeration and gives a hint about the content of the document. Values for typical types of documents in the process are predefined (e.g. a part ma

attributes.name: documentVersion
attributes.doc: The documentVersion specifies the version index of a document (see also documentNumber).

attributes.name: digitalRepresentationIndex
attributes.doc: An arbitrary change index that indicates if the digital representation (the content in VEC) of this DocumentVersion has been changed / regenerated. This can be for example an index, a timestamp or a c

attributes.name: creatingSystem
attributes.doc: The creatingSystem specifies the computer application or the machine which is used to create the document.

attributes.name: dataFormat
attributes.doc: The dataFormat specifies the convention that was used to structure the information in the document. This is useful if the DocumentVersion is a pointer to an external document, which is not contained i

attributes.name: fileName
attributes.doc: The name of the file as it appears in the VEC-Package, including the folder structure (fully qualified name) that contains this DocumentVersion . If this DocumentVersion is a link to an external docum

attributes.name: location
attributes.doc: The location is a possibility to provide a reference to the source location of the DocumentVersion (e.g. a document management system or an archive system) where the original document can be found . T

attributes.name: numberOfSheets
attributes.doc: The number of sheets contained in the document.

attributes.name: confidentialityLevel
attributes.doc: The ConfidentialityLevel of this DocumentVersion.

attributes.name: documentClassification
attributes.doc: Defines the DocumentClassifications of this DocumentVersion.

name: ExtendableElement
documentation: Abstract base class for extendable elements. Extendable elements have the possibility to define non-standard custom properties. The ExtendableElement is also used as base class for all higher-level entities in the VEC (in contrast to a StructuredPrimitive ). So, in general, referencing ExtendableElement should be possible.

name: ItemVersion
documentation: Abstract super-class for physical objects (e.g. a Terminal), virtual objects (e.g. a 150% Harness) as well as documents (e.g. a wiring diagram). In difference to AP 212 the VEC makes it only possible to describe/exchange information about Versions since Master-Objects cannot exist without one or more Versions.

attributes.name: abbreviation
attributes.doc: Room for a short name of the Item. In case of a document the attribute is wanted to contain its title.

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: Room for additional, human readable information about the ItemVersion. e.g. Buchsengehäuse 26-polig

attributes.name: companyName
attributes.doc: Defines the publishing company of the ItemVersion. The companyName is part of the main identifier of an ItemVersion together with the corresponding number (partNumber or documentNumber) and version (p

attributes.name: processingInstruction
attributes.doc: Processing instructions for the application of the part or the document.

attributes.name: changeRestriction
attributes.doc: This attribute defines if the ItemVersion is subject to some kind of change restriction. For example, some parts or document might not be changeable anymore after a certain stage in the homologation p

name: LanguageCode
documentation: Enumeration for the definition of ISO language codes. (see KBLFRM-317)

name: LocalizedString
documentation: Allows the internationalization of text contents. Attributes of the type LocalizedString normally have the multiplicity [0..*]. This means that such an attribute can have multiple values for different locales. It must not have multiple values for the same locale.

name: PartOrUsageRelatedSpecification
documentation: Base class for all specifications which are describing a PartVersion or a PartUsage . A PartOrUsageRelatedSpecification specifies a certain aspect of the described part or usage (e.g. general technical part information, connector housing aspects or wire aspects).

attributes.name: specialPartType
attributes.doc: The specialPartType allows the specification of subclassifications for a PartOrUsageRelatedSpecification (e.g. different types of connector housings).

name: PartVersion
documentation: A PartVersion is unique identifier for a part in a company context. A part can be any components within a vehicle. The PartVersion is one of the three anchors for PDM information in the VEC. All technical information about a PartVersion is contained in one or more documents. These describing elements are normally referencing to the PartVersion.

attributes.name: partNumber
attributes.doc: The partNumber is the major identifier of a PartVersion. The format is user defined and respectively company specific. For all VEC-documents a PartVersion-instance can be trusted to be identical if th

attributes.name: partVersion
attributes.doc: The partVersion specifies the version index of a part (see also partNumber).

attributes.name: primaryPartType
attributes.doc: The primary type of the part defines the type of the part (e.g. ConnectorHousing , Fixing , etc.) Since the VEC supports dual use parts (e.g. Fixing & WireProtection ) the primary part type is necessa

attributes.name: isPreferredPart
attributes.doc: Flags a part as "preferred" by the means of being a preferred part out of a group of parts with identical technical properties. The preferred part should be used, if the other properties of a couple o

attributes.name: preferredUseCase
attributes.doc: Contains a part description from the point of view of the preferred use case. Defines the function for which the part was initially designed. (e.g. "Grommet for Hatch", "...passenger compartment"). Th

attributes.name: aliasId
attributes.doc: Room to specify additional identifiers for the PartVersion. This field must not be used for alternative PartNumbers. It is intended for identifiers others than PartNumbers, such as human readable iden

attributes.name: nature
attributes.doc: The nature specifies how the PartVersion can be used in the different processes or the significance of the PartVersion in the process. The nature of a PartVersion is normally inherent and does not cha

attributes.name: partNumberType
attributes.doc: Specifies the classification of the part number associated with this PartVersion , indicating its semantic role within the BOM methodology of the issuing process (see PartNumberType for more details).

name: PrimaryPartType
documentation: The primary type of the part defines the type of the part (e.g. ConnectorHousing, Fixing, etc.) Since the VEC supports dual use parts (e.g. Fixing & WireProtection) the primary part type is necessary to define which specification associated to part is the primary character of the part. Therefore, all primary part types correspond to a PartOrUsageRelatedSpecification (e.g. ConnectorHousing --> ConnectorHousingSpecification). The primary part type ' Other ' is used if the PartVersion is not furthe

name: RoutableElement
documentation: A RoutableElement is an element that can be routed, which mean it is possible to assign it to a Path in the Topology.

name: SheetOrChapter
documentation: Documents can be structured into sheets or chapters. Since it is possible, that one document describes a couple of parts it is necessary to be able to specify which sheet, or chapter contains the description of which part. (see KBLFRM-308)

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: The identification of the sheet or chapter within the document. This value must be distinct within the context of a document.

attributes.name: sheetNumber
attributes.doc: The sheetNumber is the major identifier of a SheetOrChapter. The format is user defined and respectively company specific. This field has to be used if a SheetOrChapter has its own "DocumentNumber".

attributes.name: sheetVersion
attributes.doc: The sheetVersion specifies the version index of a sheet (see also sheetNumber)

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: Room for additional, human readable information about the SheetOrChapter.

attributes.name: sheetFormat
attributes.doc: Defines the format of the SheetOrChapter. This is an alias for a specific sheet / paper size (e.g. DINA4). If both attributes are defined the SheetSize takes precedence.

attributes.name: sheetSize
attributes.doc: Defines the size of the sheet with numerical values. This is the size of the "paper", the actual drawing area might be smaller for example due to drawing frames.

name: Specification
documentation: Abstract super-class for all specifications. Every technical information exchanged with the VEC is contained in the different specializations of a specification.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the specification. The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the document containing the specification. For all VEC-documents a Specification-instance c

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: Specifies additional, human readable information about the specification.

name: VecContent
documentation: The VecContent is the XML-Root node for any VEC-Document. Note about GeneratingSystemName and GeneratingSystemVersion: Both together are intended to provide meta information to identify the generating system and its version for reasons of traceability (system is used as general term and can also be a system landscape, a highly modularized micro service architecture or a tool chain). It is not intended to provide detailed information about the composition or configuration of a system and its modu

attributes.name: vecVersion
attributes.doc: Specifies the version of the VEC used for the file.

attributes.name: generatingSystemName
attributes.doc: Specifies the name of the system that has generated the VEC-file (see note in class documentation).

attributes.name: dateOfCreation
attributes.doc: Specifies the date of creation of the VEC-file.

attributes.name: generatingSystemVersion
attributes.doc: Specifies the version of the system that has generated the VEC-file (see note in class documentation).

name: AbstractLocalizedString
documentation: Abstract super-class for Localized text values.

attributes.name: languageCode
attributes.doc: References the corresponding languageCode of the value.

attributes.name: value
attributes.doc: The value of the LocalizedString in language defined by the languageCode.

name: LocalizedTypedString
documentation: Allows the internationalization of text contents in a typed way. Attributes of the type LocalizedTypedString normally have the multiplicity [0..*]. This means that such an attribute can have multiple values for different locales and types. It must not have multiple values for the same locale and type.

attributes.name: type
attributes.doc: Defines the type of the LocalizedTypedString . This allows the definition of a more detailed semantic than the semantic of the attribute itself with the type LocalizedTypedString. Agreed type values a

name: PartSubstitutionSpecification
documentation: A PartSubstitutionSpecification defines a set of PartVersions that can be used alternatively, due to an incomplete specification for the 150% product description. For a concrete wiring harness only on valid PartVersion remains. The selection logic for valid PartVersions is not included in the VEC. A PartSubstitutionSpecification can be used for example tubes or ring terminals, where a part of the specification is known at design time, but not yet the complete specification. For tubes for example

name: PartNature
documentation: OpenEnumeration that defines the nature of a PartVersion . The nature specifies how the PartVersion can be used in the different processes or the significance of the PartVersion in the process.

name: DocumentType
documentation: Defines the predefined DocumentTypes of a PartVersion. A certain DocumentType has normally a typical set of information that is defined within its scope. E.g. a part master document contains Specifications that are used for the description of a defined PartVersion. The content and the degree of information a DocumentType may vary in the different processes.

name: BaselineSpecification
documentation: A BaselineSpecification defines a set of ItemVersion s ( Document- and PartVersions ) that relate to each other in a certain way e.g. all parts and documents in their specific versions that contributed to a specific manufactured result. Baselines are a standard mechanism to support change, release and configuration management.

attributes.name: state
attributes.doc: Defines the state of the baseline itself (e.g. if it is finalized or work in progress).

attributes.name: content
attributes.doc: Defines the state of the content of the baseline in regard of its defined scope.

name: BaselineState
documentation: Enumeration the define the valid states of a baseline.

name: BaselineContent
documentation: Enumeration to define the state of the content of the baseline in regard of its defined scope.

name: ConfigurationConstraint
documentation: Represents a ConfigurationContraint ("When does this element exist?") for a specific application ( ApplicationConstraint) and a "configuration universe" ( VariantConfiguration.configurationType )

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the ConfigurationConstraint . The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the ConfigurableElement and does not change over the time.

name: ConfigurationConstraintSpecification
documentation: Specification container for the definition of ConfigurationConstraints .

name: DocumentClassification
documentation: A DocumentClassification is used to categorize and classify a document in the context of a document management system. It helps to maintain consistency and compliance by ensuring that documents are appropriately handled according to their classification. Classifications can be used for example to define retention periods or disposal dates. A classification is defined by a Key in a corresponding ReferenceSystem .

attributes.name: key
attributes.doc: The Key of the DocumentClassification in the corresponding classification reference system.

attributes.name: referenceSystem
attributes.doc: The identification of the classification reference system, which is defining possible values and the semantic of DocumentClassification keys.

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: On optional human readable description of the classification (e.g. the name or clear text, for example "max. 99 Years").

name: ConfidentialityLevel
documentation: Defines different levels of confidentiality for DocumentVersions.

name: ResourceVersion
documentation: A ResourceVersion is unique identifier for a resource in a company context. Resources are elements used to produce, handle or service a harness, e.g. tools or machines, which do not end up in the product (see PartVersion ). The ResourceVersion is one of the three anchors for PDM information in the VEC.

attributes.name: resourceNumber
attributes.doc: The ResourceNumber is the major identifier of a ResourceVersion . The format is user defined and respectively company specific. For all VEC-documents a ResourceVersion-instance can be trusted to be id

attributes.name: resourceVersion
attributes.doc: The ResourceVersion specifies the version index of a resource (see also ResourceNumber ).

attributes.name: primaryResourceType
attributes.doc: The primary type of the resource defines the type of the resource. In a future version of the VEC the PrimaryResourceType might correspond to Specifications describing the ResourceVersion (see Primary

name: PrimaryResourceType
documentation: The primary type of the resource defines the type of the resource. In a future version of the VEC the PrimaryResourceType might correspond to Specifications describing the ResourceVersion (see PrimaryPartType ).

name: PartNumberType
documentation: Specifies the classification of a part number associated, indicating its semantic role within the BOM methodology of the issuing process. This enables the distinction between different types of part numbers, such as those referencing actual physical parts and those used to represent virtual constructs or implementation logic. In some cases, positions in the bill of material are created to express specific aspects of the product structure, even though they do not (directly) refer to a concrete pa

name: ChangeRestrictionType
documentation: The ChangeRestrictionType defines the reason for a changeRestriction (see ItemVersion.changeRestriction for more details) .

name: CustomProperty
documentation: Abstract base class for custom properties. Basically, a custom property is key / value pair. The key (propertyType) defines the meaning of the value. A custom property can either be a simple value (string), a numerical value or a value range.

name: NumericalValueProperty
documentation: A custom property with a numerical value. (see KBLFRM-319)

attributes.name: value
attributes.doc: Defines the value of the CustomProperty.

name: SimpleValueProperty
documentation: A custom property with a simple value (string).

attributes.name: value
attributes.doc: Defines the value of the CustomProperty.

name: ValueRangeProperty
documentation: A custom property with a value range. (see KBLFRM-319)

attributes.name: value
attributes.doc: Defines the value of the CustomProperty.

attributes.doc: Defines the value of the CustomProperty.

name: BooleanValueProperty
documentation: A custom property with a Boolean value.

attributes.name: value
attributes.doc: Defines the value of the CustomProperty.

name: DateValueProperty
documentation: A custom property with a date value.

attributes.name: value
attributes.doc: Defines the value of the CustomProperty.

name: DoubleValueProperty
documentation: A custom property with a double value.

attributes.name: value
attributes.doc: Defines the value of the CustomProperty.

name: IntegerValueProperty
documentation: A custom property with an integer value.

attributes.name: value
attributes.doc: Defines the value of the CustomProperty.

name: ComplexProperty
documentation: A custom property that represents a tuple of values.

name: AbstractSlot
documentation: An AbstractSlot represents a geometrical location in a connector housing that can contain or group one or more cavities . This grouping can happen in two different ways: Directly , via a Slot , where the slot is an inseparable part of the connector housing , formed during the manufacturing process. Indirectly , via a ModularSlot , which serves as a placeholder where other connector housings (modules) can be inserted during assembly. The AbstractSlot is primarily relevant on the mating side of th

attributes.name: slotNumber
attributes.doc: Specifies the number of the slot. This must be unique within a ConnectorHousingSpecification.

name: AntennaSpecification
documentation: Specification of the electrological aspects of an antenna.

attributes.name: fMin
attributes.doc: Specifies the minimum operating frequency of the antenna.

attributes.name: fMax
attributes.doc: Specifies the maximum operating frequency of the antenna.

attributes.name: impedance
attributes.doc: Specifies the impedance of the antenna.

name: BatterySpecification
documentation: Specification of the electrological aspects of a battery.

attributes.name: u
attributes.doc: Specifies the nominal voltage of the battery.

attributes.name: i
attributes.doc: Specifies the current the battery provides.

attributes.name: iCool
attributes.doc: Specifies the battery's current in cool state.

attributes.name: capacity
attributes.doc: Specifies the power capacity of the battery.

name: Cavity
documentation: A cavity is a defined space in a connector housing for location of an electrical terminal or cavity plug or seal. A cavity may also be empty.

attributes.name: available
attributes.doc: Defines whether the cavity is available for contacting. If the cavity is not available, it means that it is completely closed.

attributes.name: cavityNumber
attributes.doc: Provides an identifier for the cavity. The cavity number needs to be unique within a Slot .

attributes.name: hasIntegratedTerminal
attributes.doc: Defines whether the cavity has an integrated terminal (for example an IDC cavity) or if an additional terminal is required. If this attribute is "true", the cavity can reference a TerminalSpecificatio

name: CavityPlugSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of cavity seals. A cavity plug is a watertight non-electrical object to fill an empty cavity.

name: CavitySealSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of cavity seals. A CavitySeal is a watertight non-electrical object to fill a populated Cavity. A CavitySeal is normally used at a WireEnd within the crimp of a terminal.

attributes.name: wireElementOutsideDiameter
attributes.doc: Specifies a range of valid wire diameters to which the cavity seal fits.

attributes.name: wireReceptionType
attributes.doc: Specifies the wireReceptionType to which the cavity seal fits.

attributes.name: insideDiameter
attributes.doc: Defines the inside diameter in the relaxed state for a cavity seal.

name: CavitySpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of cavities.

attributes.name: angle
attributes.doc: Specifies the angle against two planes of the connector housing a terminal used in this cavity can be buckled.

deprecated.reason: Replaced by the more meaningful mechanism TerminalTypes.

attributes.name: geometry
attributes.doc: Defines the geometry of a cavity in the sealing area (crimp end).

attributes.name: cavityDimension
attributes.doc: Specifies the dimension of the cavity in the sealing area of the cavity (crimp end), not in the contacting area (box end). The Height of a cavity is defined as the dimension of cavity in the direction

attributes.name: minWireElementOutsideDiameter
attributes.doc: Specifies the minimum diameter a wire is allowed to have to fit into the cavity. This definition is necessary, since wires that are too small might cause movements and in acceptable torsion forces on

attributes.name: maxWireElementOutsideDiameter
attributes.doc: Specifies the maximum diameter a wire is allowed to have to fit into the cavity.

attributes.name: primaryLockingType
attributes.doc: Specifies if the cavity has a primary locking and of what type it is.

attributes.name: sealable
attributes.doc: Specifies if the cavity is sealable.

attributes.name: compatibleTerminalType
attributes.doc: Defines a list of terminal types that are compatible to this CavitySpecification.

attributes.name: cavitySealingLength
attributes.doc: Defines the length of the sealing area in the cavity.

name: Coding
documentation: Specifies the coding of a slot or a connector housing.

attributes.name: coding
attributes.doc: Specifies the name of the coding.

name: ConductorCurrentInformation
documentation: The ConductorCurrentInformation specifies the maximum current for which a conductor is approved. As the maximum current is dependent from the voltage and the environment temperature it is modelled as a class and not only as an attribute.

attributes.name: maxCurrent
attributes.doc: The maximum current value.

attributes.name: environmentTemperature
attributes.doc: The environment temperature for which this maximum current value is applicable.

attributes.name: voltage
attributes.doc: The voltage for which this maximum current value is applicable.

name: ConductorSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of conducting properties of a WireElement.

attributes.name: crossSectionArea
attributes.doc: Specifies the cross-section area of the conductor (e.g. 0,5 mm²). The cross-section area is a nominal value, which refers to the conducting properties of the conductor normalized to the properties of

attributes.name: massInformation
attributes.doc: Specifies the mass information of the conductor. In most cases this mass information is known as copper weight and is normally specified as mass per length (e.g. gram per meter).

attributes.name: material
attributes.doc: Specifies the material of the conductor.

attributes.name: resistance
attributes.doc: Specifies the electrical resistance of the conductor. In most cases this is specified as resistance per length (e.g. Ohm per meter).

attributes.name: structure
attributes.doc: Specifies the structure of the conductor according to ISO 6722-1 for ConductorSpecifications with Type = Stranded. Should only be used for ConductorSpecifications with type=Stranded.

attributes.name: type
attributes.doc: Specifies the type of the conductor, e.g. if it is rigid or stranded.

attributes.name: numberOfStrands
attributes.doc: Specifies the number of individual strands used to construct the conductor. If the conductor is solid than the number of strands would be one. This value indicates the total number of strands forming

attributes.name: platingMaterial
attributes.doc: Specifies the plating material of the conductor.

attributes.name: strandDiameter
attributes.doc: Specifies the diameter of a single strand in the conductor.

attributes.name: voltageRange
attributes.doc: Specifies the voltageRange for which the conductor is approved.

attributes.name: transmissionMedium
attributes.doc: Specifies the type of the transmission medium for the conductor.

outgoing_relations.doc: Specifies the approved maximum currents for the conductor.

name: ConnectorHousingSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of connector housings. A connector housing consists of a one or more slots. In the means of the VEC, a connector housing can be a conventional connector housing, a contact module or a connector shell.

attributes.name: averageWireLengthAddOn
attributes.doc: Specifies the average wire length add on for this connector.

attributes.name: voltageRange
attributes.doc: Specifies the allowed voltage range for the connector housing.

attributes.name: coupleable
attributes.doc: Defines whether the connector is coupleable or not. Connectors that are coupleable can be used in an inline position. Connectors that are not coupleable can be connected only to an ECU or something si

attributes.name: connectorPositionAssurance
attributes.doc: If true the ConnectorHousing has a connector position assurance (CPA). A CPA is some sort of feature of a connector, which ensures that the connector in its correctly assembled position with its matin

attributes.name: connectorPositionAssuranceType
attributes.doc: Defines the type of the connector position assurance. This is only valid of connectorPositionAssurance = true.

attributes.name: outletDirection
attributes.doc: Defines the OutletDirection for wires. This attribute is defined as an OpenEnumeration .

attributes.name: lockingType
attributes.doc: Defines the type of locking of this connector against its counterpart.

name: CoreSpecification
documentation: Defines the properties of a circular conductor (core) which are specific for them.

attributes.name: outsideDiameter
attributes.doc: Specifies the outside diameter of the core.

name: EEComponentSpecification
documentation: Base-class for the specification of electrological components, which are connected to the harness. Usually, electrological components are not part of the harness e.g. a fuse, a switch or a control device. All EEComponents can have one or more HousingComponents which are possible interfaces for the connection to a harness.

attributes.name: powerConsumption
attributes.doc: Specifies the PowerConsumptions of this EEComponentSpecification. This refers to the internal power consumption of this E/E-component, not the power-consumption that might occur indirectly over other

attributes.name: voltageRating
attributes.doc: The voltageRating of an EEComponentSpecification indicates the maximum voltage of the circuit for which the E/E component (e.g. a fuse) is designed to operate safely.

name: FillerSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of filler elements in the wire.

attributes.name: material
attributes.doc: Specifies the material of the filler.

attributes.name: diameter
attributes.doc: Specifies the diameter of the filler.

name: FuseSpecification
documentation: Specification of the electrological aspects of a fuse.

attributes.name: fuseType
attributes.doc: The geometric type of a fuse.

attributes.name: iMax
attributes.doc: Specifies the maximum electric current tolerated by the fuse.

attributes.name: characteristic
attributes.doc: The characteristics of a fuse design refers to how rapidly the fuse responds to various current overloads.

name: GeneralTechnicalPartSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of common properties for technical parts.

attributes.name: colorInformation
attributes.doc: Specifies the color of the part.

attributes.name: massInformation
attributes.doc: Specifies the overall mass of the part per Unit of quantity (e.g. g/piece or g/meter...)

attributes.name: materialInformation
attributes.doc: Specifies the material of a part with the syntax and nomenclature of an arbitrary reference system. Multiple Material entries in this attribute are only allowed to express the same value in the differ

attributes.name: materialComposition
attributes.doc: Parts and components are often composed from a material-mix. The MaterialComposition allows the definition of the various Material s in a part and their mass. For example, the proportion of copper or

attributes.name: robustnessProperties
attributes.doc: Specifies the robustness of a part.

attributes.name: temperatureInformation
attributes.doc: Specifies valid temperatures for a part.

attributes.name: fitRate
