name: ComponentNodeViewItem
documentation: A ComponentNodeViewItem represents a ComponentNode within a ConnectionViewSpecification and defines its position within the layout.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the ComponentNodeViewItem . The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the ConnectionViewSpecification .

attributes.name: gridSquare
attributes.doc: Specifies the grid square in which the ComponentNodeViewIt em is placed (e.g. E/40).

name: Signal
documentation: Specifies a signal.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the Signal. The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the SignalSpecification.

attributes.name: signalName
attributes.doc: Name of the Signal, which is not guaranteed to be unique and is normally function oriented.

attributes.name: clampName
attributes.doc: Specifies the name of the clamp e.g. KL15, KL30, KL31.

attributes.name: aliasId
attributes.doc: Specifies additional identifiers for the Signal .

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: A human readable description of the signal.

attributes.name: signalInformationType
attributes.doc: Specifies the information type of the signal.

attributes.name: signalTransmissionMediumType
attributes.doc: Specifies the type of the transmission medium for the signal.

attributes.name: signalForm
attributes.doc: Specifies the form of the signal.

attributes.name: signalCurve
attributes.doc: Specifies the curve of the signal.

attributes.name: dataRate
attributes.doc: Defines the data rate of the signal. This applies only to signals with signalType = 'information ' and signalInformationType = 'digital' . For the numerical value, an appropriate IECUnit combination s

name: SignalSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of a list of valid signals.

name: NominalVoltage
documentation: OpenEnumeration defines the nominal voltage levels currently known and used in vehicles.

name: CartesianVector
documentation: Abstract super class for vectors, either 2D or 3D.

name: GeometryNode
documentation: A GeometryNode is the geometric representation of a TopologyNode. A TopologyNode may be represented by more than one GeometryNodes, but only within different BuildingBlockSpecification2D/3D. That means, in a single BuildingBlockSpecification a TopologyNode shall only be represent once (or not). A GeometryNode is either a GeometryNode2D or a GeometryNode3D.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the GeometryNode. The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the corresponding BuildingBlockSpecification. For all VEC-documents a GeometryNode-instance

attributes.name: aliasId
attributes.doc: Specifies additional identifiers for the GeometryNode.

name: GeometrySegment
documentation: A GeometrySegment is the geometric representation of a TopologySegment. A TopologySegment may be represented by more than one GeometrySegments, but only within different BuildingBlockSpecification2D/3D. That means, in a single BuildingBlockSpecification a TopologySegment shall only be represent once (or not). Furthermore, the definition of the GeometrySegment shall be consistent to the definition in the TopologySpecification. That means, that a GeometrySegment shall have those GeometryNodes as s

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the GeometrySegment. The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the corresponding BuildingBlockSpecification. For all VEC-documents a GeometrySegment-ins

attributes.name: aliasId
attributes.doc: Specifies additional identifiers for the GeometrySegment.

name: LengthClassification
documentation: Enumeration for the definition of a LengthClassification.

name: NodeType
documentation: Enumeration for the definition of the type of a TopologyNode.

name: SegmentCrossSectionArea
documentation: Specifies the cross-section area of a segment. For the data exchange the cross-section area is used and not the diameter, because the diameter is only a valid measure for circular segments. For circular segments, the diameter and the cross-section area can be translated into each other without the loss of information. attributes.name: area
attributes.doc: Specifies the value of the cross-section area of the segment.

attributes.name: valueDetermination
attributes.doc: Specifies the method for determination of the value.

attributes.name: crossSectionAreaType
attributes.doc: Specifies the type of the cross-section area of the segment. Different types are for example needed to differentiate between the designed space of a segment and the required space (e.g. calculated fro

name: SegmentForm
documentation: Enumeration for the definition of the SegmentForm.

name: SegmentLength
documentation: Specifies the length of a TopologySegment . The length of a TopologySegment is defined as the length of the centerline of the segment. Attributes of the type SegmentLength normally have the multiplicity [0..*]. This means that such an attribute can have SegmentLength-entries for different classifications. It must not have multiple entries with the same classification.

attributes.name: length
attributes.doc: Specifies the length of the TopologySegment.

attributes.name: classification
attributes.doc: Specifies the classification of the segment length.

name: TopologyGroupSpecification
documentation: A TopologyGroupSpecification defines a new Topology based on the grouped Topologies. (see KBLFRM-240)

name: TopologyNode
documentation: A TopologyNode is a point in the Topology where TopologySegments are starting and ending.

attributes.name: aliasId
attributes.doc: Specifies additional identifiers for the TopologyNode. Example: TopologyNode Ids may vary from one CAD system export to another. Therefore, the CAD system Id is improper for identification attribute.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the TopologyNode. The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the TopologySpecification. For all VEC-documents a TopologyNode-instance can be trusted to b

attributes.name: matchingPointId
attributes.doc: Specifies an identifier that can be used for matching TopologyNodes that belong to different TopologySpecifications and are actually representing the same node. Example: There are two TopologySpecif i

attributes.name: processingInstruction
attributes.doc: Specifies processing instructions for the TopologyNode.

attributes.name: nodeType
attributes.doc: Specifies the type of the TopologyNode. A Node can either be an EndNode, a Junction or an Inliner.

name: TopologySegment
documentation: A TopologySegment is a distance in the Topology where no intermediate electrical contacts appear. If a Topology contains routed wires, then the wire at the beginning of a TopologySegment must be the same as in the ending. TopologySegments are a logical construct to describe the physical representation of a wiring harness topology. Therefore, a TopologySegment is only valid if it has a physical manifestation. TopologySegments with a length of 0 or less do not have a physical manifestation and are

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the TopologySegment. The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the TopologySpecification. For all VEC-documents a TopologySegment-instance can be truste

attributes.name: form
attributes.doc: Specifies the form of the TopologySegment. A TopologySegment can either be circular or noncircular.

attributes.name: aliasId
attributes.doc: Specifies additional identifiers for the TopologySegment. Example: TopologySegment Ids may vary from one CAD system export to another. Therefore, the CAD system Id is improper for identification attri

attributes.name: processingInstruction
attributes.doc: Specifies processing instructions for the TopologySegment.

name: TopologySpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of a topology. A topology consists of TopologyNodes, TopologySegments.

name: TopologyZone
documentation: A TopologyZone divides a topology in different sections / design spaces. A TopologyZone may be subdivided in further TopologyZone . There can be multiple reasons for creating an orthogonal sectioning on a Topology . Therefore, TopologyZones can be overlapping.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the Zone (normally the name). The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the TopologySpecification. For all VEC-documents a Zone-instance can be trusted

attributes.name: type
attributes.doc: The type of the TopologyZone. Valid values are defined in an OpenEnumeration.

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: Specifies additional, human readable information about the zone.

attributes.name: ambientTemperature
attributes.doc: Defines the ambient temperature that can occur in this zone. This can result in specific requirements for the used components.

attributes.name: requiredRobustnessProperties
attributes.doc: Defines the robustness properties that are required in this zone. This can result in specific requirements for the used components (e.g. the ability for sealing).

name: SegmentCrossSectionAreaType
documentation: Defines valid values the type of the cross-section area of a TopologySegment , since a TopologySegment can have different cross section areas with different meanings in the process.

name: TopologyZoneSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of TopologyZones.

name: ZoneAssignment
documentation: A ZoneAssignment defines that a specific TopologySegment is affected by the TopologyZone. If a coverage is defined, only the parts of the Segment that have a coverage are affected. If no coverage is defined, the whole segment is affected.

name: ZoneCoverage
documentation: A ZoneCoverage defines an area on a TopologySegment that lies within a TopologyZone. The area is defined with two Locations . Locations are the same mechanism that is used to define placements for components. The area that is in the TopologyZone is the area between the two locations. However, there are some restrictions for the definition of the locations. All locations

name: TopologyZoneType
documentation: There can be various reasons to define TopologyZones. These can be differentiated with these type literals.

name: NodeMapping
documentation: Defines the relationship of an inner node to its outer topology. The relationship to the outer topology is expressed with a Location .

name: SegmentMapping
documentation: Defines the relationship of an inner segment to its outer topology. The relationship to the outer topology is expressed with a Path.

name: TopologyMappingSpecification
documentation: A TopologyMappingSpecification allows the definition of hierarchical topologies. It relates an outer topology with an enclosed inner topology.

name: Path
documentation: Describes a path in the topology. A Path is a continuous way through a topology without interruptions, defined by an ordered list of TopologySegments .

name: NodeLocation
documentation: Specifies a TopologyNode as a Location.

name: Location
documentation: A Location specifies a distinct position on a topology. Locations can be used for the placement of components or for the definition of Dimensions.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the Location. The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the PlacementSpecification.

attributes.name: matchingId
attributes.doc: Specifies an identification for matching the location with a reference point of component (e.g. a cable channel).

name: AnchorType
documentation: Enumeration for the definition of AnchorType of the SegmentLocation.

attributes.name: anchor
attributes.doc: Specifies if the location on the TopologySegment is defined as on offset relative to the startNode of the TopologySegment or the endNode.

name: SegmentLocation
documentation: Specifies a point on a TopologySegment as a Location.

attributes.name: offset
attributes.doc: Specifies the offset / distance of the Location to the anchor of the location.

attributes.name: anchor
attributes.doc: Specifies if the location on the TopologySegment is defined as on offset relative to the startNode of the TopologySegment or the endNode.

name: TopologyBendingRestrictionSpecification
documentation: A TopologyBendingRestrictionSpecification can be used to define TopologyBendingRestrictions.

name: TopologyBendingRestriction
documentation: As the name implies, a TopologyBendingRestriction defines restrictions on the bendability a path in the Topology. There are multiple reasons, why such restrictions exist, for example: There is a bending restriction for a wire in the segment. The number of wires and the segment diameter is such, that excessive bending causes intolerable torsion forces on wires in the segment. Other technical reasons Since these restrictions can be determined using a variety of methods the VEC provides a concept t

attributes.name: minBendRadiusDynamic
attributes.doc: Specifies the minimum bend radius for the restricted path, if it is used in a dynamic environment, where it is bended repeatedly (e.g. in the grommet of the back door).

attributes.name: minBendRadiusStatic
attributes.doc: Specifies the minimum bend radius for the restricted path, if it is used in a static environment, where it is bended once during installation. After that it remains unchanged in its bended position du

name: UsageConstraint
documentation: Specifies a constraint of the possible usages for PartVersion or PartUsages. UsageConstraints are of part master data information. UsageConstraints specify general restrictions for the application of a PartVersion or PartUsage (e.g. a certain period of time in which the part is allowed to be used). (see KBLFRM-229)

attributes.name: type
attributes.doc: Defines if the usage constraint is positive (allowance) or negative (denial).

attributes.name: fromDate
attributes.doc: Specifies the lower bound of the time period to which the usage constraint applies.

attributes.name: toDate
attributes.doc: Specifies the upper bound of the time period to which the usage constraint applies.

attributes.name: fromSerialNumber
attributes.doc: Specifies the lower bound of a serial number range to which the usage constraint applies.

attributes.name: toSerialNumber
attributes.doc: Specifies the upper bound of a serial number range to which the usage constraint applies.

attributes.name: projectPhase
attributes.doc: Specifies the project phases to which the usage constraint applies.

attributes.doc: In the production logistics of complex products (like vehicles), the control of operation and cancellation dates of changes, features, components or the like is usually not carried out via concrete da

attributes.name: toEffectivityControlKey
attributes.doc: See FromEffectivityControlKey.

name: UsageConstraintSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of usage constraints. The associated UsageConstraints are restricting the possible usages of the associated PartVersions and PartUsages.

name: UsageConstraintType
documentation: Enumeration for the definition of the type of a UsageConstraint. Valid values are A llow and Deny .

name: UsageNode
documentation: A UsageNode represents a position in an abstract vehicle. For example, the "Head Light Left". UsageNodes belong to the master data, and they are defined on some companywide level. They can be used to enforce consistent naming over different projects and different development streams (e.g. between Geometry and Electrologic). A UsageNode can be realized by different elements in the VEC (e.g. NetworkNode, OccurrenceOrUsage, TopologyNode, ComponentNode ).

attributes.name: abbreviation
attributes.doc: Specifies an abbreviation of the UsageNode . Normally this a human readable short name.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the UsageNode . The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the context. For all VEC-documents a UsageNode-instance can be trusted to be the same if the c

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: Specifies additional, human readable information about the UsageNode .

attributes.name: usageNodeType
attributes.doc: Defines the type of the UsageNode. The type determines how the UsageNode is handled in the latter processes.

name: UsageNodeSpecification
documentation: A UsageNodeSpecification is a container for the specification of UsageNodes.

name: UsageNodeType
documentation: Enumeration for the different types of UsageNodes.

name: VariantCode
documentation: VariantCodes are defining the literals on which VariantConfiguration are stated. Possible VariantCodes might be different for steering types, optional equipment, engine-power class.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the variant code. This is also the literal value for the VariantCode, which shall be used in the logisticControlExpressions of VariantConfigurations.

attributes.name: aliasId
attributes.doc: Room to specify additional identifiers for the VariantCode.

attributes.name: abbreviation
attributes.doc: Room for a human readable short name, title etc. of the VariantConfiguration.

attributes.name: codeType
attributes.doc: Allows the classification of a VariantCodes.

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: On optional human readable description of the variant code.

name: VariantCodeSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of variant codes.

name: VariantConfiguration
documentation: A variant configuration defines a condition with which it is possible to express the inclusion or exclusion of ConfigurableElements in different variants of a product. A VariantConfiguration can reference another VariantConfiguration as baseInclusion . In this case, a VariantConfiguration can only be satisfied if its baseInclusion is also satisfied.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the variant configuration. The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the specification and does not change over the time.

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: On optional human readable description of the variant configuration.

attributes.name: logisticControlString
attributes.doc: Specifies a logisticControlString which can be used if the variant management is not done by Boolean logic.

attributes.name: logisticControlExpression
attributes.doc: Specifies a logisticControlExpression expressed as Boolean term.

attributes.name: configurationType
attributes.doc: Allows the classification of a VariantConfiguration. (see KBLFRM-250, KBLFRM-314, KBLFRM-290)

name: VariantConfigurationSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of variant configurations.

name: VariantGroup
documentation: With a VariantGroup it is possible to group VariantCodes. The semantic of this grouping should be defined with the groupType (e.g. composition, choice, etc.).

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the variant code.

attributes.name: aliasId
attributes.doc: Room to specify additional identifiers for the VariantGroup.

attributes.name: abbreviation
attributes.doc: Room for a human readable short name, title etc. of the VariantGroup.

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: On optional human readable description of the variant group.

attributes.name: groupType
attributes.doc: Allows the classification of a VariantGroups into different types. For example: - composition (e.g. winter package) - choice (e.g. right hand / left hand driving). Agreed literals for this attribute a

name: VariantGroupSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of variant groups.

name: ApplicationConstraintSpecification
documentation: Specification for the definition of application constraints. The associated ApplicationConstraints are restricting the possible usages of the associated ConfigurableElements .

name: ApplicationConstraint
documentation: An ApplicationConstraint defines a condition with which it is possible to express the inclusion or exclusion of ConfigurableElements in different variants of a product. The ApplicationConstraint is focused to express validity rules based on time periods or elements of the product hierarchy in a concise way (attributes and relationships). It is complementary to the VariantConfiguration which expresses validity rules based on control strings. An ApplicationConstraint can reference another Applicat

attributes.name: type
attributes.doc: Defines if the application constraint is positive (allowance) or negative (denial). If the ApplicationConstraint has a baseInclusion that baseInclusion shall define the same type.

attributes.name: fromDate
attributes.doc: Specifies the lower bound of the time period to which the application constraint applies.

attributes.name: toDate
attributes.doc: Specifies the upper bound of the time period to which the application constraint applies.

attributes.name: fromSerialNumber
attributes.doc: Specifies the lower bound of a serial number range to which the application constraint applies.

attributes.name: toSerialNumber
attributes.doc: Specifies the upper bound of a serial number range to which the application constraint applies.

attributes.name: projectPhase
attributes.doc: Specifies the project phases to which the application constraint applies.

attributes.name: fromEffectivityControlKey
attributes.doc: In the production logistics of complex products (like vehicles), the control of operation and cancellation dates of changes, features, components or the like is usually not carried out via concrete da

attributes.name: toEffectivityControlKey
attributes.doc: See FromEffectivityControlKey.

name: ApplicationConstraintType
documentation: Enumeration for the definition of the type of an ApplicationConstraints. Valid values are Allow and Deny .

name: VariantGroupType
documentation: Defines valid values for the type of VariantGroups.

name: VariantStructureSpecification
documentation: Specification to define any hierarchical structure on variant groups (e.g. by the means of a functional organization). The hierarchy starts with a single root node.

name: VariantStructureNode
documentation: VariantStructureNodes can be used to define a hierarchical structure on VariantGroups . Every VariantStructureNodes can reference VariantGroups and VariantStructureNodes as children.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the VariantStructureNode .

attributes.name: aliasId
attributes.doc: Room to specify additional identifiers for the VariantStructureNode .

attributes.name: abbreviation
attributes.doc: Room for a human readable short name, title etc. of the VariantStructureNode .

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: On optional human readable description of the VariantStructureNode .

name: VariantCodeType
documentation: OpenEnumeration for the available types of the variant codes.

name: VariantConfigurationType
documentation: Defines an OpenEnumeration for VariantConfigurationTypes. The configuration type defines in which "variant code universe" the logistic control expression is defined.

name: RequirementsConformanceSpecification
documentation: A RequirementsConformanceSpecification can be used to express the conformance of a PartVersion (or a group of PartVersions ). The PartVersions to which this RequirementsConformanceSpecification applies are expressed through the describedPart reference.

name: RequirementsConformanceStatement
documentation: A RequirementsConformanceStatement states that the PartVersions referenced by the parent RequirementsConformanceSpecification satisfy or do not satisfy the requirements defined in the associated DocumentVersion (via the requirementsSpecification association) .

attributes.name: satisfies
attributes.doc: Defines if the describedParts satisfy (satisfy = true) or explicitly fail (satisfy = false) to conform with the requirementsSpecification .

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: A free text description / additional information / comment for the RequirementsConformanceStatement.

name: LocalGeometrySpecification
documentation: A LocalGeometrySpecification is responsible to create a relationship between the 3D model of a component (e.g. a connector, a cable duct or a fixing) and entities of the VEC. The 'Local' in the name refers to the fact that all definitions within this specification are 'local' to the 3D model of a specific component (a component in a library, not in a specific usage). Specifically, it defines a transformation to transform the BoundingBox of a component into to coordinate system of the component a

name: PlacementPointPosition
documentation: Defines the position of a PlacementPoint within the coordinate system of the component. PlacementPoints are points where a component is attached to a TopologySegment. Therefor a PlacementPointPosition can define a tangent vector (in the coordinate system of the component) for a segment that is connected to the PlacementPoint.

attributes.name: tangent
attributes.doc: A vector in the direction of the tangent on the TopologySegment that is attached to the PlacementPoint represented by this instance. The vector is defined in the coordinate system of the 3D model of t

name: MeasurePointPosition
documentation: Defines the position of a MeasurementPoint within the coordinate system of the component. MeasurementPoint onto which dimension can be defined .

name: LocalPosition
documentation: A LocalPosition defines the position of a relevant point of component within the coordinate system of the component.

name: PinWireMappingSpecification
documentation: A PinWireMappingSpecification can be used create variance free mappings between a wire (represented by the contact point) and the pin of an E/E component. This is a possibility to create a shortcut in the model between a wire and its connected E/E-component (e.g. a fuse) that might be only indirectly connected to a wire (e.g. via a fuse and relay carrier). This is a relevant information for e.g. the validation of fusing. See the Pin Wire Mapping Diagram for more details.

name: PinWireMappingPoint
documentation: The PinWireMappingPoint creates a single variance free mapping between a ContactPoint and a PinComponentReference within a PinWireMappingSpecification (more details there) .

name: AssignmentGroup
documentation: An AssignmentGroup is a concept that allows the clustering of arbitrary elements in ways that are orthogonal to hierarchical and semantic structure of the VEC.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the AssignmentGroup. The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the specification.

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: Specifies additional, human readable information about the AssignmentGroup .

name: AssignmentGroupSpecification
documentation: Specification that contains AssignmentGroups .

name: DocumentRelatedAssignmentGroup
documentation: A DocumentRelatedAssignmentGroup allows the creation of traceability links to elements in a DocumentVersion for a set of VEC objects. The semantic of the traceability link is defined by the DocumentRelationType.

attributes.name: relatedIdentification
attributes.doc: If this group relates to a specific element in the relatedDocumentVersion the identifier of the element is defined in this attribute (e.g. a requirements number).

name: FunctionalAssignmentGroup
documentation: The FunctionalAssignmentGroup clusters elements that contribute to a specific function or a functional aspect. With such a group, certain functional requirements can be associated.

attributes.name: functionalRequirements
attributes.doc: Functional requirements that apply to the members of this group.

name: FunctionalRequirement
documentation: Allows the definition of functional requirements in an enumerable way (e.g. conformance to a certain ASIL level). Attributes of this type have the multiplicity of [0..*]. The following restrictions apply: For a combination of type & referenceSystem only a single value is allowed. For single type For a specific type and different references systems, multiple values are allowed. However, they must express the same semantic value. For different types multiple values are allowed.

attributes.name: type
attributes.doc: The type defines to which category a requirement belongs (e.g. Functional Safety).

attributes.name: referenceSystem
attributes.doc: The reference system identifies the system in which the values are defined (e.g. ISO26262)

attributes.name: value
attributes.doc: The value that represents the functional requirement (e.g. ASIL D).

name: FunctionalStructureNode
documentation: FunctionalStructureNodes can be used to define a hierarchical structure on FunctionalAssignmentGroups . Every FunctionalStructureNode can reference FunctionalAssignmentGroups and FunctionalStructureNodes as children.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the FunctionalStructureNode.

attributes.name: aliasId
attributes.doc: Room to specify additional identifiers for the FunctionalStructureNode .

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: On optional human readable description of the FunctionalStructureNode .

attributes.name: abbreviation
attributes.doc: Room for a human readable short name, title etc. of the FunctionalStructureNode .

name: FunctionalStructureSpecification
documentation: Specification to define any hierarchical structure on functional assignment groups (e.g. by the means of a functional organization). The hierarchy starts with a single root node.

name: SignalGraphSpecification
documentation: Specification to define a list of SignalGraphs in a vehicle network.

name: SignalGraph
documentation: A SignalGraph is a directed graph of elements in the vehicle network that participate in the transmission of a signal / function / power / ground etc. A SignalGraph is expected to be at least a unilaterally connected graph, meaning it contains a directed path from u to v or a directed path from v to u for every pair u and v of SignalGraphNodes in the SignalGraph.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the SignalGraph . The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the SignalGraphSpecification .

attributes.name: aliasId
attributes.doc: Defines additional identifiers for the SignalGraph .

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: Specifies additional, human readable information about the SignalGraph .

name: SignalGraphEdge
documentation: A SignalGraphEdge connects two SignalGraphNodes directed from "fromNode" to "toNode" and represents the direction of signal flow.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the SignalGraphEdge . The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the SignalGraph .

name: SignalGraphNode
documentation: A SignalGraphNode represent some physical element that participates in the signal transmission related to a SignalGraph . If the representedElement fails or is not present in a network, some paths in the SignalGraph maybe disrupted.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the SignalGraphNode . The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the SignalGraph .

name: SignalGraphRelation
documentation: A SignalGraphRelation represents a directed association between two SignalGraphs . The direction of the relationship is defined as " from" --> "to" and the semantic is defined by the type.

attributes.name: identification
attributes.doc: Specifies a unique identification of the SignalGraphRelation . The identification is guaranteed to be unique within the SignalGraphSpecification .

attributes.name: aliasId
attributes.doc: Defines additional identifiers for the SignalGraphRelation .

attributes.name: description
attributes.doc: Specifies additional, human readable information about the SignalGraphRelation .

attributes.name: type
attributes.doc: Defines the semantic of the relationship between the "from"- and "to"-SignalGraph.

name: SignalGraphRelationType
documentation: This OpenEnumeration defines a set of predefined semantics for the SignalGraphRelation between two SignalGraph ("from" & "to").

name: ReusageSpecification
documentation: A ReusageSpecification enables the traceability of information reuse or derivation in different contexts. A mapping between the source ( template ) and the destination ( usage ) model elements is created with the contained Reusage -Elements. For more information see Chapter "Information Reuse".

name: Reusage
documentation: A Reusage defines a link for of information reuse between model elements that are reused in a different context. The source of information ( template ) and the destination ( usage ) shall have the same type (VEC model class). For more information see Chapter "Information Reuse".
